stem: An adult client's serum magnesium level is below the laboratory reference interval. Which complication is associated with magnesium deficiency?

options.A: Ventricular arrhythmias and cardiac electrical instability can occur with magnesium deficiency, particularly when other electrolyte disturbances are also present.
options.B: Progressive atrioventricular conduction slowing with central nervous system and respiratory depression is more characteristic of magnesium excess than deficiency.
options.C: Neuromuscular and cardiac manifestations are not expected from magnesium deficiency when another electrolyte value happens to remain within its reference interval.
options.D: A below-reference magnesium concentration indicates magnesium excess from renal retention and therefore predicts toxicity rather than an arrhythmic complication.

rationale: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories guidance states that hypomagnesemia reliably indicates magnesium deficiency. Mayo describes magnesium deficiency as being associated with cardiac disorders including ventricular arrhythmias, increased sensitivity to digoxin, coronary artery spasm, and sudden death, as well as neuromuscular and neuropsychiatric abnormalities. In contrast, hypermagnesemia can prolong atrioventricular conduction and severe magnesium toxicity can cause CNS depression, cardiac arrest, and respiratory arrest. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize hypomagnesemia as evidence of magnesium deficiency and identify ventricular arrhythmias as an important associated cardiac complication.
source_version_date: Current Mayo test catalog; live page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Clinical Information: magnesium deficiency is associated with cardiac disorders including ventricular arrhythmias, increased digoxin sensitivity, coronary artery spasm, and sudden death; concurrent neuromuscular/neuropsychiatric symptoms may occur. Reference Values: >17 years 1.7–2.3 mg/dL. Cautions: hypomagnesemia reliably indicates magnesium deficiency.
source_claim_supported: A below-reference serum magnesium result represents hypomagnesemia/magnesium deficiency, which is associated with ventricular arrhythmias and other cardiac and neuromuscular complications.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — interpret laboratory results, recognize abnormal findings and potential complications, and initiate appropriate follow-up.
correction_summary: Removed the distractor-only absolute wording and balanced all alternatives around clinically relevant magnesium-deficiency versus magnesium-excess effects.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — current Mayo guidance directly links magnesium deficiency to ventricular arrhythmias and distinguishes hypermagnesemia/toxicity effects; A uniquely answers the stem.
